title: When does cross-pollination quietly become convergence?
question: Can TurtleBlock AI notice when repeated traceable perturbations are gradually collapsing genuinely different branches into de facto convergence without scoring similarity, blocking exchange, or inventing a machine-defined amount of acceptable difference?
why_now: The September 22 Cross-Branch Perturbation Envelope answers the prior horizon at the single-transfer boundary: a question, observation, or constraint may cross as a proposal while source and target histories remain separate, upstream human provenance stays recoverable, human authority governs any target change, and neither world evidence nor metrics authorize transfer. The remaining risk is longitudinal rather than transactional. A sequence of individually valid transfers could still make branches converge in practice. The Wait-a-minute pass also exposed a recurring agency pattern: Selective Attention separates noticing from interruption, TurtleAsk separates ask formation from surfacing, and cross-branch perturbation separates discovery from application. The next edge is whether the system can make cumulative influence inspectable without becoming a machine judge of how different branches ought to remain.
inputs: current repository after Cross-Branch Perturbation contract implementation
current Build Log and September 18 reconciliation history
Sanders research ontology and seven established Critical Techno Constructivism operational domains
fresh OpenAI, NVIDIA, Minecraft Education, and MIT Media Lab primary-source signals
absence of an authorized consent-safe TRY IT visitor research read path
possible_possibles: Represent a cumulative transfer lineage without assigning a similarity score or a convergence threshold.
Let humans mark that two branches are intentionally becoming more alike, intentionally remaining different, or simply evolving without a declared relation.
Surface provenance-only warnings when one branch has received many proposals from another while leaving interpretation to people.
Treat reciprocal borrowing as a potentially generative relationship rather than assuming influence is contamination.
Use synthetic self-play only to generate hostile longitudinal transfer fixtures; synthetic activity never decides acceptable branch difference.
x_factor: whoooo knooooowwwssssssssssss — what if two branches become more interesting precisely because they borrow from each other and still refuse to agree?
constraints: No machine-defined similarity threshold may become a pedagogical or design verdict.
Repeated transfer must not silently establish a canonical branch, winner, merge objective, or correction narrative.
Human participants retain authority to accept, rewrite, reject, ignore, or reinterpret cross-branch proposals.
Source and target lineage, including upstream human provenance when applicable, remain recoverable.
Synthetic self-play remains synthetic_self_play and has no production authority or human-learning evidence status.
No generalized persistent personal memory is introduced by this horizon.
No autonomous production self-modification or self-retraining is authorized.
No new CTC domain is promoted without explicit human scholarly judgment.

ontology_mappings.rationale: Repeated exchanges can recursively alter constructed trajectories while preserving who or what introduced each difference.
Plural branches should remain sources of future possibility rather than being optimized toward one synthesized state.
The horizon concerns effects that only become visible across multiple cycles of transfer and revision.
Longitudinal influence remains interpretable only if each proposal, decision, and revision keeps its source identity.
Borrowing, divergence, failure, and recombination may all be generative without requiring convergence.
Any system observation about cumulative influence must remain material for human interpretation rather than a verdict.

ctc_mappings.rationale: People decide whether accumulating influence supports or distorts the inquiry they are pursuing.
Repeated cross-pollination may open or close questions over time without automatically resolving them.

ctc_mappings.domain: Technology as Tool to Think With
ctc_mappings.rationale: Transfer lineage becomes a manipulable representation for thinking about influence rather than an optimization score.
A changing branch trajectory may later support reflection, but convergence or divergence is not itself evidence of learning.
Longitudinal traces can support reflection on why branches changed and which borrowed elements mattered.
Judgments about acceptable similarity, originality, borrowing, and influence are power-bearing and culturally situated.
The question concerns exchange among trajectories without turning collaboration into compulsory sameness.

uncaptured_residue.observation: Repeated individually legitimate transfers may create de facto convergence without any explicit merge event.
uncaptured_residue.reason_unmapped: This is a longitudinal governance phenomenon spanning collaboration, provenance, inquiry, and representation rather than a clear new pedagogical domain.

uncaptured_residue.observation: Reciprocal influence can be generative rather than erosive; preserving difference should not become an anti-collaboration purity rule.
uncaptured_residue.reason_unmapped: The tension between productive borrowing and provenance-preserving plurality may be adequately representable through relationships and human reflection, but stronger theoretical naming is premature.

wait_a_minute_connection.summary: Selective Attention says noticing is not permission to interrupt; TurtleAsk says forming an ask is not permission to surface it; cross-branch perturbation now says discovering useful difference is not permission to apply it. The recurring structure is initiative without automatic authority.
wait_a_minute_connection.uncertainty: This may be a recurring implementation principle rather than a distinct Sanders concept; human scholarly judgment should decide whether it deserves stronger theoretical status.
